entries.title: Molykote D-321 R Anti-Friction Coating Spray
entries.dupontTitle: MOLYKOTE® D-321 R Anti-Friction Coating Spray
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote D-321 R Anti-Friction Coating Spray — Aerosol: An air cured anti-friction coating filled with molybdenum disulfide and graphite.
entries.descriptionLong:
Aerosol: An air cured anti-friction coating filled with molybdenum disulfide and graphite.

Features & benefits

  • Air drying

Applications

For metal/metal combinations with slow to medium fast movements and high loads. Suitable for the permanent lubrication of highly stressed sliding guides with low sliding speeds, oscillating movements or intermittent operation. Used for improving the running-in process and for lubrication under high vacuum and at extreme temperatures. Used successfully for cylinder-head bolts, toaster guides, car mirror adjustment mechanisms, high voltage switches, for the running-in of highly stressed gear wheel. Emergency Lubricant for parts of the rotor head of wind energy installations and for groove-free cold extrusion of steel.

Composition

  • Technology: Organic Binder, Solids, Solvent
  • Solid lubricants: MoS2, graphite

Available pack sizes

  • 400 ml can - 12 per carton

About this type of lubricant

An anti-friction coating is a bonded dry film: solid lubricant particles held in a resin binder, applied like a paint and then cured, air-dried or heat-cured. Once cured it is a permanent dry lubricating layer, typically 5-20 µm thick, that does not attract dust, does not migrate and does not need re-application.

How to choose

Choose a coating where oil or grease cannot be used or cannot be maintained: dusty and abrasive environments, clean assemblies, sealed-for-life mechanisms, plastic-on-metal contact, and points that are inaccessible after assembly. Surface preparation determines whether the coating lasts at all — the substrate must be clean and, for heat-cured grades, correctly pretreated. Check the cure temperature against what the component can survive before specifying; air-cured grades exist precisely for parts that cannot be baked.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. Our engineers will confirm the grade against your application and operating conditions before you commit.

entries.title: Molykote 1122 Chain Grease Spray
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 1122 Chain Grease Spray — Aerosol Form: NLGI Grade 2-3 - Polyisobutylene-based grease with a base oil viscosity of 1500 cSt at 40°C, no thickener, uses molybdenum disulfide and graphite as solid lubricants.
entries.descriptionLong:
Aerosol Form: NLGI Grade 2-3 - Polyisobutylene-based grease with a base oil viscosity of 1500 cSt at 40°C, no thickener, uses molybdenum disulfide and graphite as solid lubricants.

Features & benefits

  • Emergency lubrication

Applications

Used for initial lubrication of chains with hollow pins equipped with grease nipples (e.g., high tenter clamp chains in the textile industry and conveyor chains in food sterilizer units). Also used for gear drives and open gears; sliding bearings operating at low speeds and high temperatures, such as bearings in drying systems; and calendering machines used in various industrial processes.

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil, Polyisobutene (PIB)
  • Thickener: None
  • Solid lubricants: MoS2, graphite

Available pack sizes

  • 400 ml can - 12 per carton

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

entries.title: Molykote CU-7439 Plus Paste Spray V1
entries.dupontTitle: MOLYKOTE® CU-7439 Plus Paste Spray V1
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote CU-7439 Plus Paste Spray V1 — Aerosol: A mineral oil based anti-sieze paste formulated with copper as the solid lubicant and enhanced corrosion protection.
entries.descriptionLong:
Aerosol: A mineral oil based anti-sieze paste formulated with copper as the solid lubicant and enhanced corrosion protection.

Features & benefits

  • Excellent adhesion to metal surfaces

Applications

Disc brakes, brake cams, brake guides, flange seals, adjuster screws, and threaded connections; vehicle assembly and maintenance (e.g., truck drum brakes); in steel works, glass manufacturing, refineries, and petrochemical facilities; and on agricultural and marine vehicles.

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil, Solids
  • Solid lubricants: Solid Lubricants

Available pack sizes

  • 400 ml can - 12 per carton

About this type of lubricant

A paste is a very high concentration of solid lubricant in a small amount of carrier oil — closer to a thick suspension than to a grease. It is used where a grease would be squeezed out: assembly and running-in of tight metal-to-metal fits, press fits, splines, threaded fasteners and anti-seize duty. The solids stay behind on the surface after the carrier is gone, which is the point.

How to choose

Pastes are for assembly and slow, heavily loaded contact, not for continuous high-speed lubrication — use a grease for that. For threaded joints, the coefficient of friction is the number that matters, because it is what a torque figure assumes; a paste that changes friction changes the clamping force the bolt actually achieves. Copper- and metal-filled pastes should not be used on stainless or on joints where galvanic corrosion is a risk.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. entries.title: Molykote 33 Light Extreme Low Temperature Grease
entries.dupontTitle: MOLYKOTE® 33 Light Extreme Low Temperature Grease
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 33 Light Extreme Low Temperature Grease — NLGI Grade 1 - Silicone-based grease with a base oil viscosity of 76 cSt at 40°C, lithium-thickened, with no solid lubricants.
entries.descriptionLong:
NLGI Grade 1 - Silicone-based grease with a base oil viscosity of 76 cSt at 40°C, lithium-thickened, with no solid lubricants.

Features & benefits

  • Good oxidation resistance

Applications

Ideal for use in roller and conveyer equipment, control cables, electric motors, photographic equipment, optical equipment, measurement equipment, etc. Is also used in refrigerators or freezer equipment.

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone
  • Thickener: Lithium
  • Solid lubricants: None

Available pack sizes

  • 3.6 kg pail - 4 per carton
  • 18 kg pail
  • 25 kg pail
  • 100g-10CTN, tub

About this type of lubricant

A grease is a base oil held in a thickener, so it stays where it is put instead of draining away. The thickener (lithium, lithium complex, calcium sulfonate, polyurea or a clay) sets the upper service temperature and the water resistance; the base oil — mineral, PAO, ester, silicone or PFPE — sets the low-temperature behaviour and the chemical compatibility. Molykote greases add solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE, which carry the load in the moments when the oil film is too thin to: start-up, shock load, slow oscillation.

How to choose

Match four things in order: the service temperature range, the speed and load, whether the point sees water or chemicals, and what the grease touches. Plastic and elastomer components rule out many mineral-oil greases; food-contact points need an H1-registered grade; slow, heavily loaded or oscillating joints are where the solid-lubricant content earns its cost. NLGI grade is consistency, not quality — a lower number is softer and pumps more easily, a higher number stays put in an open or vertical point. Never mix thickener types in the same point: incompatible thickeners can soften and run out.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. faqs.question: How do I choose the right grease?
faqs.answer: Match four things in order: the service temperature range, the speed and load, whether the point sees water or chemicals, and what the grease touches. Plastic and elastomer components rule out many mineral-oil greases; food-contact points need an H1-registered grade; slow, heavily loaded or oscillating joints are where the solid-lubricant content earns its cost. NLGI grade is consistency, not quality — a lower number is softer and pumps more easily, a higher number stays put in an open or vertical point. Never mix thickener types in the same point: incompatible thickeners can soften and run out.

entries.title: Molykote D-6818 Anti-Friction Coating
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote D-6818 Anti-Friction Coating — A sprayable anti-friction coating with excellent wearing resistance to withstand extremely high loading pressure under low viscosity oil condition.
entries.descriptionLong:
A sprayable anti-friction coating with excellent wearing resistance to withstand extremely high loading pressure under low viscosity oil condition.

Features & benefits

  • Suitable for spray coating

Applications

For metal/metal combinations involving slow to medium speeds and low to medium loads. Suitable for lubrication of heavily loaded friction contacts involving low to high speeds, in direct contact with motor oils, gasoline, diesel or grease. Used in automotive or industrial applications like metal parts for engine bearing, plain bearing, washer, etc.

Composition

  • Technology: Organic Binder, Solids, Solvent
  • Solid lubricants: Graphite, MoS2

Available pack sizes

  • 1.1 kg can - 10 per carton

About this type of lubricant

An anti-friction coating is a bonded dry film: solid lubricant particles held in a resin binder, applied like a paint and then cured, air-dried or heat-cured. Once cured it is a permanent dry lubricating layer, typically 5-20 µm thick, that does not attract dust, does not migrate and does not need re-application.

How to choose

Choose a coating where oil or grease cannot be used or cannot be maintained: dusty and abrasive environments, clean assemblies, sealed-for-life mechanisms, plastic-on-metal contact, and points that are inaccessible after assembly. Surface preparation determines whether the coating lasts at all — the substrate must be clean and, for heat-cured grades, correctly pretreated. Check the cure temperature against what the component can survive before specifying; air-cured grades exist precisely for parts that cannot be baked.

entries.descriptionLong:
High-performance paste in aerosol form. It is particularly effective as a running-in Lubricant. This product features a low coefficient of friction immediately upon application, without burnishing.

Features & benefits

  • Excellent protection against fretting wear and corrosion

Applications

Primarily designed as a running-in Lubricant for plain bearings, splines, gears, cams and ways, and because of its low coefficient of friction, as a Lubricant for movable screws, threaded spindles and lead screws. It can

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil
  • Solid lubricants: MoS2, white solids

Available pack sizes

  • 400 ml can - 12 per carton

About this type of lubricant

A paste is a very high concentration of solid lubricant in a small amount of carrier oil — closer to a thick suspension than to a grease. It is used where a grease would be squeezed out: assembly and running-in of tight metal-to-metal fits, press fits, splines, threaded fasteners and anti-seize duty. The solids stay behind on the surface after the carrier is gone, which is the point.

How to choose

Pastes are for assembly and slow, heavily loaded contact, not for continuous high-speed lubrication — use a grease for that. For threaded joints, the coefficient of friction is the number that matters, because it is what a torque figure assumes; a paste that changes friction changes the clamping force the bolt actually achieves. Copper- and metal-filled pastes should not be used on stainless or on joints where galvanic corrosion is a risk.

entries.title: Molykote D-3484 Anti-Friction Coating
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote D-3484 Anti-Friction Coating — Heat-hardening anti-friction coating
entries.descriptionLong:
Heat-hardening anti-friction coating

Features & benefits

  • Combines excellent lubricating effect with good corrosion protection

Applications

Sliding coating for metal/metal combinations with slow to moderately fast movements and moderate to high loads. Suitable for the permanent lubrication of friction pairs with high compressive stress and low speeds and also where – for technical reasons or because the risk of soiling is unacceptable – oil or Grease cannot be used. Used successfully for pawls of safety cutouts, carburetor springs, lorry coupling sleeves, toothed gears, and parts of car safety belts and car-boot lock parts. Bolts and levers in tractors and construction machines.

Composition

  • Technology: Organic Binder, Solids, Solvent
  • Solid lubricants: MoS2, graphite

Available pack sizes

  • 500 g can - 10 per carton
  • 5 kg pail

About this type of lubricant

An anti-friction coating is a bonded dry film: solid lubricant particles held in a resin binder, applied like a paint and then cured, air-dried or heat-cured. Once cured it is a permanent dry lubricating layer, typically 5-20 µm thick, that does not attract dust, does not migrate and does not need re-application.

How to choose

Choose a coating where oil or grease cannot be used or cannot be maintained: dusty and abrasive environments, clean assemblies, sealed-for-life mechanisms, plastic-on-metal contact, and points that are inaccessible after assembly. Surface preparation determines whether the coating lasts at all — the substrate must be clean and, for heat-cured grades, correctly pretreated. Check the cure temperature against what the component can survive before specifying; air-cured grades exist precisely for parts that cannot be baked.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. Our engineers will confirm the grade against your application and operating conditions before you commit.

entries.dupontTitle: MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC (High Voltage Insulator Coating) Compound
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 3099 HVIC (High Voltage Insulator Coating) Compound — NLGI Grade 2-3, charcoal, used primarily as a high voltage insulator coating.
entries.descriptionLong:
NLGI Grade 2-3, charcoal, used primarily as a high voltage insulator coating.

Features & benefits

  • Easy to use In addition to a high level of flashover resistance, MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound incorporates an arc-resistant filler that inhibits arc growth. This helps protect the insulator from glaze damage when the coating’s water repellency is significantly diminished and arcing is experienced. Another benefit of MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound is the ease of handling. The compound is easy to spread, not stringy, and shows good adhesion to properly prepared insulators

Applications

Used to give a protective coating to electrical insulators. The consistency of the compound provides easy application to the required coating thickness. The gray opaque appearance of MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound makes it easy to ensure a uniform and complete coating is obtained. For more detailed application information, see technical datasheet.

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone
  • Thickener: Silica

Available pack sizes

  • 4.5 kg pail
  • 22.6 kg pail

About this type of lubricant

Compounds are silicone-based, non-melting greases used less for friction than for sealing, insulating and protecting. Typical duty is dielectric insulation and moisture-sealing of electrical connections, lubrication and sealing of rubber and plastic parts, valve and O-ring assembly, and vacuum sealing.

How to choose

Compounds do not carry high mechanical loads — if the point is a loaded bearing or gear, a grease or paste is the right family. The silicone caution applies here too: a compound on a surface that will later be painted, bonded or printed will cause the coating to fail. On rubber and elastomer components, confirm compatibility with the specific elastomer — silicone compounds are excellent on most, and wrong on silicone rubber itself.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. entries.focusKeyword: Molykote 3099 HVIC (High Voltage Insulator Coating) Compound

faqs.question: What is this product used for?
faqs.answer: Used to give a protective coating to electrical insulators. The consistency of the compound provides easy application to the required coating thickness. The gray opaque appearance of MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound makes it easy to ensure a uniform and complete coating is obtained. For more detailed application information, see technical datasheet.

faqs.question: What are the main performance benefits?
faqs.answer: Easy to use In addition to a high level of flashover resistance, MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound incorporates an arc-resistant filler that inhibits arc growth. This helps protect the insulator from glaze damage when the coating’s water repellency is significantly diminished and arcing is experienced. Another benefit of MOLYKOTE® 3099 HVIC Compound is the ease of handling. The compound is easy to spread, not stringy, and shows good adhesion to properly prepared insulators.

faqs.question: What is it based on?
faqs.answer: Silicone, thickened with Silica.

faqs.answer: Compounds do not carry high mechanical loads — if the point is a loaded bearing or gear, a grease or paste is the right family. entries.title: Molykote 7514 Grease
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 7514 Grease — Synthetic (PAO/ester) Grease especially for intermediate transmissions of starter motors
entries.descriptionLong:
Synthetic (PAO/ester) Grease especially for intermediate transmissions of starter motors

Features & benefits

  • Wide service-temperature range: -40 to +180°C (-40 to 356°F)

Applications

Used in automotive components, etc., due to its superior properties for plastic/metal sliding, rubber/metal sliding, and rubber/plastic sliding.

Composition

  • Technology: Ester, Polyalphaolefin (PAO)
  • Thickener: Lithium Complex

Available pack sizes

  • 50 kg pail

About this type of lubricant

A grease is a base oil held in a thickener, so it stays where it is put instead of draining away. The thickener (lithium, lithium complex, calcium sulfonate, polyurea or a clay) sets the upper service temperature and the water resistance; the base oil — mineral, PAO, ester, silicone or PFPE — sets the low-temperature behaviour and the chemical compatibility. Molykote greases add solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE, which carry the load in the moments when the oil film is too thin to: start-up, shock load, slow oscillation.

How to choose

Match four things in order: the service temperature range, the speed and load, whether the point sees water or chemicals, and what the grease touches. Plastic and elastomer components rule out many mineral-oil greases; food-contact points need an H1-registered grade; slow, heavily loaded or oscillating joints are where the solid-lubricant content earns its cost. NLGI grade is consistency, not quality — a lower number is softer and pumps more easily, a higher number stays put in an open or vertical point. Never mix thickener types in the same point: incompatible thickeners can soften and run out.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. A high-performance lubricant designed for the food and beverage industry. It is a mineral-based lubricant thickened with aluminum complex and additive package designed for broad use. It is an excellent choice where an NSF H1 status lubricant is required.

Features & benefits

  • • Excellent lubricating properties

Applications

Multipurpose lubrication of mechanical components such as bearings, chains, gears and slides in food and beverage processing facilities.

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil
  • Thickener: Aluminum Complex

Available pack sizes

  • 380G-10CTN
  • 180KG-drum

About this type of lubricant

A grease is a base oil held in a thickener, so it stays where it is put instead of draining away. The thickener (lithium, lithium complex, calcium sulfonate, polyurea or a clay) sets the upper service temperature and the water resistance; the base oil — mineral, PAO, ester, silicone or PFPE — sets the low-temperature behaviour and the chemical compatibility. Molykote greases add solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE, which carry the load in the moments when the oil film is too thin to: start-up, shock load, slow oscillation.

How to choose

Match four things in order: the service temperature range, the speed and load, whether the point sees water or chemicals, and what the grease touches. Plastic and elastomer components rule out many mineral-oil greases; food-contact points need an H1-registered grade; slow, heavily loaded or oscillating joints are where the solid-lubricant content earns its cost. NLGI grade is consistency, not quality — a lower number is softer and pumps more easily, a higher number stays put in an open or vertical point. About this type of lubricant

A grease is a base oil held in a thickener, so it stays where it is put instead of draining away. The thickener (lithium, lithium complex, calcium sulfonate, polyurea or a clay) sets the upper service temperature and the water resistance; the base oil — mineral, PAO, ester, silicone or PFPE — sets the low-temperature behaviour and the chemical compatibility. Molykote greases add solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE, which carry the load in the moments when the oil film is too thin to: start-up, shock load, slow oscillation.

How to choose

Match four things in order: the service temperature range, the speed and load, whether the point sees water or chemicals, and what the grease touches. entries.title: Molykote L-5030 Semi-Dry Lubricant
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote L-5030 Semi-Dry Lubricant — A liquid, semi-dry lubricant formulated without intentionally added PFAS, compatible with a wide range of plastics and elastomers. It rapidly forms a thin, semi-dry lubricating film on the substrate to facilitate assembly, reduce assembly force and improve component fit, minimize wear and fretting corrosion, and deliver reliable, long-lasting lubricity.
entries.descriptionLong:
A liquid, semi-dry lubricant formulated without intentionally added PFAS, compatible with a wide range of plastics and elastomers. It rapidly forms a thin, semi-dry lubricating film on the substrate to facilitate assembly, reduce assembly force and improve component fit, minimize wear and fretting corrosion, and deliver reliable, long-lasting lubricity.

Features & benefits

  • • Translucent to semi-translucent appearance after solvent evaporated

Applications

Suitable for a wide range of applications where a semi-dry lubricating film is required, including consumer electronic devices, electrical connector metal contacts, O‑rings, seals, and other plastic or elastomer‑based components.

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone

Available pack sizes

  • 0.6KG-10CTN

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

After being coated, it forms a white, semi-dry film that is not sticky like grease.

Features & benefits

  • Compatible with many plastics and elastomers

Applications

Lubrication of sliding parts of cameras; audio-visual equipment; precision appliances; office equipment such as printers, copiers and fax machines.

Composition

  • Technology: Perfluoropolyether (PFPE)
  • Solid lubricants: PTFE

Available pack sizes

  • 1 kg can - 10 per carton

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

entries.descriptionLong:
Product viscosity grade is documented at 25°C.

Features & benefits

  • Excellent high-temperature stability

Applications

  • Automotive fan clutches

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone

Available pack sizes

  • 1000 kg IBC

About this type of lubricant

These are fluids rather than greases — silicone, synthetic hydrocarbon and mineral oils used where the lubricant has to flow, damp, release or carry heat away. The range covers damping fluids for controlled movement in switches and hinges, gear and chain oils, release fluids for moulding, and heat-transfer and dielectric fluids.

How to choose

Viscosity is the first decision and it is temperature-dependent: an ISO viscosity grade or a measured viscosity at 40 °C is what to quote, not a description. For damping, the viscosity is the specification — it sets how much resistance the user feels. Check compatibility before anything else on silicone fluids: silicone migrates, and a trace on a surface that later has to be painted, bonded or printed will reject the coating.

entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 316 Silicone Release Fluid — Release agent for many food & beverage and industrial applications.
entries.descriptionLong:
Release agent for many food & beverage and industrial applications.

Features & benefits

  • Meets FDA 21 CFR 175.300 regulations

Applications

For food and beverage industry processing:

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone
  • Thickener: Silica

Available pack sizes

  • 355 g bottle - 12 per carton
  • 14.1 kg pail
  • 283G-12CTN

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

entries.title: Molykote M Gear Oil Additive
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote M Gear Oil Additive — Dispersion of molybdenum disulfide in mineral oil used in extreme pressure applications.
entries.descriptionLong:
Dispersion of molybdenum disulfide in mineral oil used in extreme pressure applications.

Features & benefits

  • High load-carrying capacity at slow speeds

Applications

Typical applications include:

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil
  • Solid lubricants: MoS2

Available pack sizes

  • 17.2 kg pail

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 112 High Performance Lube/ Sealant — NLGI Grade 3, translucent white, used primarily as a general-purpose valve lubricant with high mechanical shear stability and high temperature range.
entries.descriptionLong:
NLGI Grade 3, translucent white, used primarily as a general-purpose valve lubricant with high mechanical shear stability and high temperature range.

Features & benefits

  • Nonmelting

Applications

This product is similar to MOLYKOTE® 111 Valve Lubricant and Sealant and is used in applications where a higher degree of mechanical stability is desired. For more detailed application information, see technical datasheet.

Composition

  • Technology: Silicone
  • Thickener: Silica
  • Solid lubricants: Silica

Available pack sizes

  • 18.1 kg pail

About this type of lubricant

Compounds are silicone-based, non-melting greases used less for friction than for sealing, insulating and protecting. Typical duty is dielectric insulation and moisture-sealing of electrical connections, lubrication and sealing of rubber and plastic parts, valve and O-ring assembly, and vacuum sealing.

How to choose

Compounds do not carry high mechanical loads — if the point is a loaded bearing or gear, a grease or paste is the right family. The silicone caution applies here too: a compound on a surface that will later be painted, bonded or printed will cause the coating to fail. On rubber and elastomer components, confirm compatibility with the specific elastomer — silicone compounds are excellent on most, and wrong on silicone rubber itself.

entries.title: Molykote 7415 Thinner
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 7415 Thinner — Anti-friction coating thinner used to reach desirable viscosity.
entries.descriptionLong:
Anti-friction coating thinner used to reach desirable viscosity.

Features & benefits

  • Low evaporation rate

Applications

Specific diluting and cleaning solvent for the following MOLYKOTE® Anti-Friction Coatings: MOLYKOTE® D-7405 Anti-Friction Coating, MOLYKOTE® D-7409 Anti-Friction Coating and MOLYKOTE® D-7620 Anti-Friction Coating.

Composition

  • Technology: Solvent

Available pack sizes

  • 5kg pail

About this type of lubricant

An anti-friction coating is a bonded dry film: solid lubricant particles held in a resin binder, applied like a paint and then cured, air-dried or heat-cured. Once cured it is a permanent dry lubricating layer, typically 5-20 µm thick, that does not attract dust, does not migrate and does not need re-application.

How to choose

Choose a coating where oil or grease cannot be used or cannot be maintained: dusty and abrasive environments, clean assemblies, sealed-for-life mechanisms, plastic-on-metal contact, and points that are inaccessible after assembly. Surface preparation determines whether the coating lasts at all — the substrate must be clean and, for heat-cured grades, correctly pretreated. Check the cure temperature against what the component can survive before specifying; air-cured grades exist precisely for parts that cannot be baked.

entries.title: Molykote D Paste
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote D Paste — A mineral-oil-based anti-seize paste formulated with solid lubricants such as white solids - used primarily for assembly and run-in.
entries.descriptionLong:
A mineral-oil-based anti-seize paste formulated with solid lubricants such as white solids - used primarily for assembly and run-in.

Features & benefits

  • High load-carrying capacity

Applications

Sliding surfaces and friction contacts exposed to heavy loads, requiring “clean” lubrication, particularly at low speeds, and as a running-in Lubricant. Suitable for use on many friction contacts; electrical and domestic appliances, packaging and office machinery, precision instruments, and machinery in the food and beverage industry, as well as in textile and plastics processing machinery.

Composition

  • Technology: Mineral Oil
  • Thickener: Thickener
  • Solid lubricants: White Solids

Available pack sizes

  • 20.4 kg pail
  • 1KG-10CTN
  • 180KG-DRUM

About this type of lubricant

A paste is a very high concentration of solid lubricant in a small amount of carrier oil — closer to a thick suspension than to a grease. It is used where a grease would be squeezed out: assembly and running-in of tight metal-to-metal fits, press fits, splines, threaded fasteners and anti-seize duty. The solids stay behind on the surface after the carrier is gone, which is the point.

How to choose

Pastes are for assembly and slow, heavily loaded contact, not for continuous high-speed lubrication — use a grease for that. For threaded joints, the coefficient of friction is the number that matters, because it is what a torque figure assumes; a paste that changes friction changes the clamping force the bolt actually achieves. Copper- and metal-filled pastes should not be used on stainless or on joints where galvanic corrosion is a risk.

How to order

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ. Indus Hydraulics is an authorised distributor and quotes MOLYKOTE® from Dubai stock where the grade is held; less common grades ship to order. entries.title: Molykote U-N Paste
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote U-N Paste — A PAG-based anti-seize paste formulated with solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide and white solids.
entries.descriptionLong:
A PAG-based anti-seize paste formulated with solid lubricants such as molybdenum disulfide and white solids.

Features & benefits

  • Dry lubrication up to 450°C

Applications

For assembling, running-in and permanent lubrication of components that are subjected to high temperatures. MOLYKOTE® U-N Lubricant Paste is suitable for the dry lubrication of bearings (low rotary speeds), slideways and joints that are subjected to temperatures exceeding 200°C; at higher temperatures, the carrier volatilizes, leaving virtually no residue, and the remaining dry anti-friction film alone takes over the only lubrication up to +450°C – even beyond this in a protective gas atmosphere. As the paste has a synthetic oil base, it is also suitable for lubricating construction elements that consist of materials that are not resistant to mineral oils. Used successfully for roller and sliding bearings of foundry ladles and converter bearings in steel works, conveyor and driving rollers of belt conveyors, in the bearings of furnace and shuttle kilns, chains and chain conveyor rollers, for joints of ironing presses, for O-rings that are not resistant to mineral oils, lip seals, rubber and cup leathers.

entries.title: Molykote 7365 Lubolid (EXP) Additive Powder
entries.descriptionShort: Molykote 7365 Lubolid (EXP) Additive Powder — Free-flowing powder of inorganic solids for use in friction lining formulations.
entries.descriptionLong:
Free-flowing powder of inorganic solids for use in friction lining formulations.

Features & benefits

  • Reduction of fading Improvement of friction recovery

Applications

Additive Powders are suitable for use in the following applications: pads of disc brakes for passenger cars and commercial vehicles, linings for drum brakes, pads for railroad disc brakes, brake shoes for railroad wheel brakes, general industrial brake linings, and clutch linings.

Composition

  • Technology: Solids
  • Solid lubricants: blend

Available pack sizes

  • 25 kg bag

About this type of lubricant

A dispersion is solid lubricant — usually molybdenum disulfide, graphite or PTFE — suspended in a carrier oil or solvent so it can be brushed, sprayed, dipped or added to an oil system. The carrier delivers the solids to the surface and then evaporates or blends away, leaving the solid lubricant behind.

How to choose

Dispersions are used for running-in, for pre-treating surfaces before first operation, and as an additive to an existing oil charge to carry a machine through break-in or a period of marginal lubrication. Where a dispersion is added to a circulating system, confirm compatibility with the filtration first — solid lubricant particles and fine filters do not agree.

Specify the pack size and, where more than one grade shares a name, the exact grade on the RFQ.
